title: Watch the Pages deploy after a merge and re-run it once if it fails
summary: The 5xx/timeout retry with backoff, per-retry reporting, and 5xx tests (retried-then-succeeds, persistent) already exist in gh.rs, jev.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/external_calls.rs. The missing piece is the post-merge Pages step: after a PR merges, find the pages workflow run for the merged commit, wait for it, and re-run it once through the gh wrapper if it timed out or was cancelled, reporting that re-run. The audience is the repo owner running `athena land --pr`.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for the Pages re-run use the injected runner and the existing fake gh pattern.
The retry is not duplicated, because the single wrapper already handles it. The Pages step reuses it.
The external_calls_guard test keeps every gh call inside gh.rs.
One focused change adding only the missing Pages step.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Existing transient-retry behavior (Retry::STANDARD, 3 attempts, doubling backoff with jitter, ui line per retry) already meets the first and third sentences, so it is not rebuilt.

Only the Pages watch is new. Its call is a `gh api` REST call to list workflow runs for the merged commit and to POST the re-run. The wait is bounded, and a Pages failure is reported but does not undo a landed merge.
"Record each retry" is met by the existing ui report line per retry; the Pages re-run uses the same mechanism and adds no new record type.
The workflow file .github/workflows/pages.yml does not need to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core -p athena-cli`. A new test shows a Pages run that concludes `timed_out` after a merge is re-run exactly once via the gh wrapper and the run then succeeds. The test asserts that exactly one re-run call was made and that one report line names the run and the conclusion.
Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`. A new test shows a Pages run concluding `cancelled` is re-run once, and that a second failure of the re-run is reported and not re-run again (no loop).
Run `cargo test`. A test shows a Pages run that concludes `success` is not re-run, and a merge in a repository with no Pages run for the merged commit does not fail the landing.

Run `cargo test`. The existing 5xx tests still pass: one is retried and succeeds, the other keeps failing until the three attempts run out. They cover the new Pages calls too (a 5xx on the runs listing is retried), and each retry is reported.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean, and `external_calls_guard` still passes: all GitHub calls stay in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs.
A decisions entry or doc note says how the Pages watch works: the bound on waiting, a single re-run, and that the outcome is reported to the user.

out_of_scope: Changing the existing 5xx retry bounds or backoff for gh and Jev calls
Editing .github/workflows/pages.yml or enabling the Pages source setting
Re-running CI workflows other than pages
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than the reference, because the change touches the PR landing flow, which already has extensive fake-runner tests, and the Pages API sequence needs a design choice.
